status: provisional: candidates adopted for testing on 2026-11-10. Any number may apply to one pair.
scope: Unless a test says otherwise, 'chromatic colors' means the ground, figure and accent with C above 0.04.

basis.measured: Computed by tools/classify.mjs. Must be listed when the test passes and omitted when it fails.
basis.hybrid: The script suggests it, and a curator confirms or rejects it.
basis.curated: Assigned by judgement from visual evidence and context. No color test can establish it.

dimensions.label: Color temperature

classifications.label: Warm
classifications.definition: Reds, oranges, yellows, warm browns and warm-leaning neutrals.
classifications.test: Judged on the ground and figure: at least one chromatic color in the warm arc and none in the cool arc, ignoring ambiguous hues. If neither is chromatic, tinted colors (C at least 0.01) decide. The accent counts only when the pair has no temperature.

classifications.label: Cool
classifications.definition: Blues, blue-greens, cool purples and cool-leaning neutrals.
classifications.test: Judged on the ground and figure: at least one chromatic color in the cool arc and none in the warm arc, ignoring ambiguous hues. If neither is chromatic, tinted colors (C at least 0.01) decide. The accent counts only when the pair has no temperature.

classifications.label: Balanced
classifications.definition: A deliberate balance of warm and cool colors.
classifications.test: At least one color in each arc, using the same colors as Warm and Cool.

dimensions.notes: Hues from 110 to 170 (yellow-green to green) and 290 to 340 (violet) are ambiguous and receive no temperature.

dimensions.label: Saturation and intensity

classifications.label: Vibrant
classifications.definition: Strong, vivid color.
classifications.test: A chromatic color meets the vibrant floors in primary.json.

classifications.label: Muted
classifications.definition: Subdued, softened color.
classifications.test: A chromatic color is neither vibrant nor pastel.

classifications.label: Pastel
classifications.definition: Light colors with relatively low chroma.
classifications.test: A chromatic color has L at least 0.80 and C at most 0.10.

classifications.label: High Intensity
classifications.definition: Strong impact through vivid color and contrast together.
classifications.test: A vibrant color is present and the pair's WCAG ratio is at least 4.5:1, or both pair colors are vibrant.

classifications.label: Low Intensity
classifications.definition: Restrained, understated color presence.
classifications.test: No vibrant color is present and the pair's WCAG ratio is below 7:1.

dimensions.notes: Research should check whether Vibrant and Muted duplicate the flat primaries that contain those words.

classifications.label: Earthy
classifications.definition: Soil, stone, clay, sand and foliage.
classifications.test: Suggested when a chromatic color has hue 20 to 130, L 0.25 to 0.72 and C 0.03 to 0.14. A curator confirms.

classifications.label: Jewel Tones
classifications.definition: Rich, deep colors such as emerald, sapphire, ruby and amethyst.
classifications.test: A chromatic color has L 0.25 to 0.49, relative chroma at least 0.60 and C at least 0.09.

classifications.label: Natural
classifications.definition: Evokes organic materials and natural environments.
classifications.notes: Likely to overlap with Earthy, Organic and Pastoral. A merge candidate.

classifications.label: Industrial
classifications.definition: Metallic, concrete, graphite and mechanical tones.

classifications.label: Pastoral
classifications.definition: Soft countryside greens, yellows, creams and browns.
classifications.notes: Likely to overlap with Natural and Earthy. A merge candidate.

dimensions.label: Color relationships

classifications.label: Monochromatic
classifications.definition: Variations of one hue.
classifications.test: Every color with C at least 0.01 fits within one hue family, and at least two such colors exist.

classifications.label: Analogous
classifications.definition: Neighboring hues.
classifications.test: At least two chromatic colors, and the smallest arc containing their hues is more than 30 and at most 60 degrees.

classifications.label: Complementary
classifications.definition: Opposing hues.
classifications.test: Two chromatic colors differ in hue by at least 150 degrees.

classifications.label: Split Complementary
classifications.definition: A base hue with two hues adjacent to its complement.
classifications.test: Three chromatic colors where two each differ from the third by 120 to 165 degrees and from each other by 15 to 75 degrees.

classifications.label: Triadic
classifications.definition: Three hues spread around the wheel.
classifications.test: Three chromatic colors whose pairwise hue differences are all 100 to 140 degrees.

classifications.label: Tetradic
classifications.definition: Four hues forming two complementary pairs.
classifications.test: Needs four chromatic colors, so it cannot apply to a pair with one accent. Kept for research on multi-color entries.

classifications.label: Near-Neutral + Accent
classifications.definition: A mostly neutral palette with one or a few chromatic accents.
classifications.test: Ground and figure are neutral and the accent is chromatic, or exactly one pair color is chromatic and it holds at most 25% of the declared area.

dimensions.notes: Hue angles are OKLCH, which differ from RYB and HSL wheels.

dimensions.label: Contrast

classifications.label: High Contrast
classifications.definition: Strong separation between ground and figure.
classifications.test: WCAG ratio between ground and figure is at least 7:1.

classifications.label: Moderate Contrast
classifications.definition: Clear separation with some softness.
classifications.test: WCAG ratio from 3:1 up to 7:1.

classifications.label: Low Contrast
classifications.definition: Subtle separation.
classifications.test: WCAG ratio below 3:1.

classifications.label: Tonal
classifications.definition: Closely related colors that read as one family.
classifications.test: Ground and figure are within one hue family (or both neutral) and differ in L by less than 0.25. Applies alongside a ratio band.

dimensions.notes: This is visual contrast. Accessibility is checked separately against each intended use.

dimensions.label: Aesthetic character

classifications.label: Sophisticated
classifications.definition: Refined restraint that rewards attention.
classifications.notes: Merge candidate with Elegant and Luxurious.

classifications.label: Playful
classifications.definition: Informal and light-hearted, often through unexpected pairings.

classifications.label: Minimal
classifications.definition: Few colors and a lot of quiet space.

classifications.label: Elegant
classifications.definition: Graceful, poised and controlled.

classifications.label: Bold
classifications.definition: Confident, assertive color.
classifications.notes: Merge candidate with Energetic and Dramatic.

classifications.label: Luxurious
classifications.definition: Rich and indulgent.

classifications.label: Futuristic
classifications.definition: Technological and forward-looking.

classifications.label: Vintage
classifications.definition: Evokes an earlier period through aged or period color.

classifications.label: Organic
classifications.definition: Grown rather than manufactured.

classifications.label: Professional
classifications.definition: Credible, orderly and businesslike.

classifications.label: Experimental
classifications.definition: Deliberately unconventional.

classifications.label: Romantic
classifications.definition: Soft, tender and intimate.

classifications.label: Energetic
classifications.definition: Lively and kinetic.

classifications.label: Calm
classifications.definition: Settled and quiet.

classifications.label: Dramatic
classifications.definition: Theatrical, with strong tension.

dimensions.notes: Impressions, not properties. Assign from visual evidence and design context, never from the colors alone, and make no claim that a color causes the impression.

dimensions.label: Composition and application

classifications.label: Color Blocking
classifications.definition: Large, distinct, flat areas of color.

classifications.label: Gradient
classifications.definition: Gradual transitions between colors.

classifications.label: Accent-Led
classifications.definition: One or a few colors provide most of the chromatic emphasis.

classifications.label: Background-Led
classifications.definition: The ground color establishes most of the identity.

classifications.label: Section-Based
classifications.definition: Different sections use distinct color combinations.

classifications.label: Layered
classifications.definition: Colors work through overlapping surfaces and layers.

classifications.label: Image-Led
classifications.definition: Photography or imagery supplies much of the color identity.

dimensions.notes: How color is distributed. Needs visual evidence or a usage plan, which a pair of values cannot supply.
